changes: original_meaning 按拉丁语 prospectus 的 gloss 改为「向远处眺望；远景」，并点明构词（pro- 向前 + specere 看）。
semantic_path 按 Etymonline 编年重建两站（1530 年代景观义 → 1620 年代心理眺望 → 1660 年代期望义 → 1922 年有希望的人/物），how 写明从眼睛转到心里的桥。
evidence: Etymonline: "prospect (n.) early 15c., \"act of looking into the distance, condition of facing something else or a certain direction,\" from Latin prospectus \"distant view, look out; sight, faculty of sight,\" noun use of past participle of prospicere \"look out on, look forward,\" from pro \"forward\" + specere \"look at\""

Etymonline: "The meaning \"extensive view of the landscape\" is from 1530s; transferred sense of \"mental view or survey\" is from 1620s... The sense of \"person or thing considered promising\" is from 1922, from the earlier sense of \"expectation, ground of expectation,\" especially of advantage (1660s) on the notion of \"looking forward,\" hence \"anticipation.""
prospect.mechanism_sentence: prospect 是拉丁语「往前看」（pro- 向前 + specere 看）：眼前望出去的景观，转进心里就是展望——前景、可能性、期望，全从这一次「向前看」长出来。

semantic_path.how: 『往前看』从眼睛转进心里（比喻）：1530 年代先指展现在眼前的景观，1620 年代转指『心里的审视与图景』，1660 年代落到『所期望（尤其指有望得益）之物』上，1922 年连有前途的人也叫 prospect——词库『前景；期望』即这一整支。

changes: original_meaning 前溯到拉丁语 probare 的 gloss「检验，证明（合格）」：现行路径以古法语为首站、古英语 prōfian 为第二站，顺序与源流不合（两路同出拉丁语）。
semantic_path 按 Etymonline 编年重建三站（检验 → 13 世纪初证实 → 14 世纪末『证明是』）。
evidence: Etymonline: "prove (v.) c. 1200, prēven, pruven, proven \"to try by experience or by a test or standard; evaluate; demonstrate in practice,\" from Old French prover, pruver \"show; convince; put to the test\" (11c.), from Latin probare \"to make good; esteem, represent as good; make credible, show, demonstrate; test, inspect; judge by trial\"... from probus \"worthy, good, upright, virtuous.\""

Etymonline: "From early 13c. as \"render certain, put out of doubt\"... By c. 1300 as... \"prove by argument.\" ... The meaning \"be found to be (a hero, coward, etc.) by experience or trial\" is by late 14c."
Oxford: "from Latin probare 'test, approve, demonstrate', from probus 'good'."
prove.mechanism_sentence: prove 的老底是拉丁语 probare「验一验是不是好货」（probus 是「正直、合格」）：先是动手检验，后是用证据证明，再是让事实自己说话——「试」这个核心从没变过。

semantic_path.how: 英语约 1200 年入词时重在『拿标准试一试』：13 世纪初添『使确凿无疑』，约 1300 年添『以论证证明』——检验从手上走到了证据与逻辑上，词库今义『证明；证实』在此定型。
14 世纪末添不及物义：经受住考验、被发现是某样（英雄、懦夫……）——prove 从『我来证明』翻成『事实自证』（proved to be），词里那个『试』字还在起作用。

changes: original_meaning 按中古英语 podynge 约 1300 年的实义记录为「一种灌馅香肠（动物胃/肠灌肉）」，与 Etymonline 的首义记录对应；拉丁语 botellus 的 gloss「小肠」是所用器官名，不单列为原义。
semantic_path 第二站 how 补甜点义的形成路径（16 世纪袋煮食品扩展、1670 年新义落定，Etymonline 编年），替换套话。
双词源（日耳曼 *pud-『肿』说 vs 法语 boudin‹botellus 说）维持现行链条与 disputes 的未定论登记不变，本补丁不改判。
evidence: Etymonline: "pudding (n.) c. 1300, \"a kind of sausage: the stomach or one of the entrails of a pig, sheep, etc., stuffed with minced meat, suet, blood, and seasoning, boiled and kept till needed,\" perhaps from a West Germanic stem *pud- \"to swell\"... The other possibility is the traditional one... that it is from Old French boudin \"sausage,\" from Vulgar Latin *botellinus, from Latin botellus \"sausage\""

Etymonline: "The sense of \"dish consisting of flour, milk, eggs, etc., originally boiled in a bag until semi-hard, often enriched with raisins or other fruit\" had emerged by 1670, from extension to other foods boiled or steamed in a bag or sack (16c.)."
Oxford: "Middle English (denoting a sausage such as black pudding): apparently from Old French boudin 'black pudding', from Latin botellus 'sausage, small intestine'."
pudding.mechanism_sentence: pudding 出生时是一根灌满肉馅、煮好备用的肠（约 1300 年）：后来「装进袋子里煮熟的东西」都归它管，1670 年前后就变成了面糊加鸡蛋牛奶（常拌果干）的布丁——肠衣换成了布袋。
pudding.original_meaning: 一种灌馅香肠（动物的胃、肠灌肉煮成）

semantic_path.meaning: 一种灌馅香肠（动物的胃、肠灌肉煮成）
semantic_path.period: 中古英语时期（约 1300 年）

semantic_path.how: 都是『包起来煮的东西』：16 世纪 pudding 从肠衣灌的肉，扩到一切装在布袋或布里水煮、蒸熟的食物；1670 年『面粉、牛奶、鸡蛋（常加葡萄干等果料）煮至半硬』的甜点义落定（Etymonline 编年）——词库的『布丁』即此，英国人至今仍把香肠型的叫 black pudding，两义并存。

changes: original_meaning 前溯一站：现行字段直接写今义「码头」，漏了古北法语 cai 的原义『沙岸』与高卢语『围起来』的词根义（Etymonline 链）。
semantic_path 重建三站，把 1690 年代的拼写法国化单独立站说明（词义未变、读音未变）。
mechanism_sentence 重写（原句为浅述式）。
evidence: Etymonline: "quay (n.) \"landing place, place where vessels are loaded and unloaded, a wharf,\" 1690s, a spelling variant of Middle English key, keye, caye \"wharf\" (c. 1300; mid-13c. in place names), from Old North French cai (Old French chai, 12c., Modern French quai) \"sand bank,\" from Gaulish caium (5c.), from Old Celtic *kagio- \"to encompass, enclose\" (source also of Welsh cae \"fence, hedge,\" Cornish ke \"hedge\"), from PIE root *kagh- \"to catch, seize; wickerwork, fence\" (see hedge (n.)). Spelling altered in English by influence of French quai."
Oxford: "late Middle English key, from Old French kay, of Celtic origin. The change of spelling in the late 17th cent. was influenced by the modern French spelling quai."
quay.mechanism_sentence: quay 和 hedge 原是亲戚——都出自「围、栏」的老词根：围在水边的沙岸，成了装卸船只的码头；1690 年代它借了法语 quai 的拼法上身，读音却还是老样子的 key。

semantic_path.how: 『围起来的岸』贴着水，就是装卸货的地方：中古英语 key/caye 约 1300 年已专指码头——它与 hedge（篱笆）同根，都是『围』出来的东西。
义未动，只换衣裳：1690 年代拼写受现代法语 quai 影响改作 quay，发音仍沿中古的 key（/kiː/）——法式拼法，英式老音。
